slide_review.scope: Citation, flight platform, spin and radius, shared flight run and mission context.
SIBAL downward propagation for over a minute; PMMA upward burning and Coriolis deflection.
Flight SIBAL: spread rates, extinction phase, gravity and oxygen history.
Flight PMMA: non-steady base, tip rate, oxygen dip and rebound; compare the late gravity drop with the slide 44 caption.
Ground comparison and tracking limits; SIBAL width, approximate extinction timing, gravity and oxygen.
Ground PMMA: base tracking, early tip growth, Earth gravity and oxygen decline.
Fitted flight and ground rates; relative SIBAL extinction time and PMMA tip-rate comparison.

warnings: Oxygen varied during burning. Reported concentrations describe a time history, not a flammability threshold. The ground SIBAL trace stayed near 20%.
Pressure has no numerical value in these observations. NASA describes the flight chamber as being at normal pressure.
Rotation produced effective lunar gravity; Coriolis deflected the PMMA flame. No sample was burned on the lunar surface.

Flight gravity is labeled nominal 0.165 g: (2π × 11 rpm / 60)² × 1.22 m / 9.80665, using slide 12. For PMMA, slide 22 reports a decrease near 125 s. Slide 44 calls gravity approximately constant, although its plotted trace drops late. The nominal value describes the rotating phase, not the entire burn.
